overview: Black meets 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 with ...c6 and usually follows with ...d5, which transposes to the Slav or Semi-Slav; ...d5 is not forced, so Black can also set up with ...e6 or ...g6. White chooses 3.Nc3 or 3.Nf3 and the game usually becomes a Slav or Semi-Slav structure with a solid pawn on c6.

white_ideas.idea: Take space with 3.Nc3 or 3.Nf3 and e3 or e4 depending on the Slav transposition.
Play for the Catalan-style or Exchange structure if Black commits to ...d5.

black_ideas.idea: Support ...d5 with ...c6 and develop the light bishop before ...e6.
Keep options open between Slav, Semi-Slav and Indian set-ups (...g6, ...d6).

typical_structures.structure: Slav centre with pawns on c6 and d5 against c4 and d4.

character.notes: Mostly Slav and Semi-Slav territory; solid and hard to break down, though Semi-Slav branches can be sharp.

gambit.notes: No material is offered; c4 is not taken here.

soundness.notes: A transposition to the Slav, which is fully sound.

structure.notes: A move-order root; the centre is undecided until ...d5 or another set-up.

approach.notes: A move-order device into the Slav family, played at all levels.

level.notes: Needs knowledge of which Slav structure it transposes to; not a first-repertoire choice.

sublines_that_differ.name: Semi-Slav
sublines_that_differ.how: Can lead to sharper Botvinnik and Meran lines.

character.reason: The Slav-based structures are hard to break down.

structure.reason: Centre not yet decided at the root.

approach.reason: A normal move-order route into the Slav.

plans.reason: Too undecided for a characteristic plan.
